study type: Mixed-methods (Interrupted Time Series and Exploratory Qualitative study)
cohort: The study included 21,000 pregnant women who attended antenatal care at 15 public hospitals in the Sidama region, Ethiopia, before (March 2019 to February 2020) and during (March to August 2020) the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: The study found a significant monthly decrease of 0.7% in antenatal care 1 and 1.8% in antenatal care 4 during the first six months of the COVID-19 pandemic.
cross-section timing: The concurrent mixed-methods study was conducted between February 14 and May 10, 2022, using quantitative data from March 2019 to August 2020.
